distinguishing_features: Compliant low-modulus polyurethane elastomer coating on the impeller surface
Erosion mitigation via elastic impact-energy absorption and extended contact time (reducing peak contact stress)
Strain-rate-dependent damping decoupling impact velocity from surface stress
Physical surface-material substitution rather than a data-driven predictor or operating-envelope control
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce the peak contact stress from high-velocity hard-particle impacts on the impeller surface so that material removal (erosion) is slowed without altering impeller geometry or adding monitoring/control schemes.
parsed.viable_reason: Elastomer coatings are a physically sound, industrially practiced means of absorbing particle impact energy and are applicable at the stated 2-5 mm thickness and 20 m/s tip speed.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art discloses a compliant elastomer surface layer that mitigates erosion by extending contact time and lowering peak impact stress, so this mechanism is not a routine application of the cited approaches.
